transcript: One of Shakespeare’s trickiest plays is being revived in New York right now, incorporating imagery of spy surveiIIance and video game aesthetics. Coriolanus is a play that I struggle with because the arc of it is really fascinating to me, about a soldier who tries and fails to become a politician and sides with his enemy to retaliate against the people who exiled him. But the way that it's dramatized is not always as compelling to me as the overall story. So it benefits from productions that are heavily cut down, tightly paced, and extremely focused, which I don't think this production was. There is definitely a lot to chew on when it comes to the visual motifs here, drawing links but between modern surveiIIance technology and screen vioIence. But I don't think the actual mechanics of the drama support these parallels very well. VioIence and scrutiny are both central themes in this play, but not necessarily as they exist in modern day. Modern crisis of surveiIIance is one of the public being scrutinized by those in power, whereas i'd argue that Coriolanus is more about the experience of a person in power being scrutinized by the people. Likewise, most of the action focuses on Coriolanus wrestling not with tactical opponents like you would in a combat video game, but wrestling with the social and political expectations of everyone around him. So while there is some common ground to explore here, the way it's mapped on in this production rang a little dissonant to me. But if you're curious to see a production of this difficult but thought provoking Shakespeare play that's not performed all that often, it's playing right now at TFANA through March 1st.
